Hello, I bought a vacuum cleaner last month, but it doesn't work as well as I expected. I am considering returning it. Okay, first, I need to get a few details about this item. Can you give me your name, please? Yes, it's Dianne Ruddick. It's R-U-D-D-I-C-K, right? Yes, that's right. Could you tell me your mobile number? It's 4-5 double 6-3-2-1, and that's my home number. Got it, and your address, please? It's No.42, Garden Avenue. Right, now I need some information about the product. Do you remember when exactly you bought it last month? Um, let me see, there was a promotion from 26th July to 31st July, and I made the purchase on the last day. Okay, now I need to take down a few details about the problem. I highly doubt the quality of the item. Okay. I will make a note of that, and we will see what we can do. Now I need one more thing, how much did you pay when you bought it? You mentioned you made the purchase during the promotion, right? Yeah, that's right. I still got the invoice, let me check, oh, its original price was $154, but I only paid $104 for that. Okay, according to what we have talked about just now, I suggest we repair the handle and it's totally free. I don’t think this is a minor problem that can be fixed. I’m quite disappointed with the vacuum cleaner. Umm, recently we have a new type available. If you are interested, I can apply for some kind of discount for you. That works for me. Could you tell me more about the new model? Yeah, of course, this model has a reusable bag, so you needn't buy loads of plastic bags, and it's more environmentally friendly. Yeah, I guess so, but you will have to wait several days for the model with both colors. No problem, as long as it’s not a broken one, I will go for purple.

parts.transcript: Well, good evening, everyone. My name's Gary Payne, and I'll be the leader for your walking holiday in Spain. And the purpose of this evening's meeting is for us all to get to know each other in advance and for you to ask any questions you may have about the holiday. So, I'll begin by telling you a little bit about what to expect. Now, the ferry crossing from England to Santander in Spain takes about 24 hours. We'll be sailing on the Prince Regent, which was first launched in the 1980s. As well as the crew of 160, it can accommodate about 2000 people and 600 cars, and it sails at an average speed of 37 kilometers an hour. Although our mini bus will be on one of the vehicle decks in the boat, access to these decks is prohibited during the crossing. So when you leave our bus, you'll have to take everything that you're likely to need with you, like toiletries or books and magazines. In fact, it's probably a good idea to put these things in a separate bag beforehand. You shouldn't need snacks on board as meals are provided, and they're quite substantial. And if you don't feel well or get a headache, you can get tablets from me. I always carry an adequate supply. Now, once we're in Spain, we'll be based at a hostel in a small village called La Vega de Liebana, about 120 kilometers from Santander. It's a very picturesque area that's retained a lot of its traditional industry and culture. The hostel accommodations fairly simple. There are bunk beds and each room holds 4 to 8 people. But the bathrooms and showers are of a high standard. The hostel residents have the use of tennis courts nearby, if you feel like a game. We'll be given breakfast and an evening meal at the hostel. In general, the hostel is relaxed, but there are a few rules which the owners enforce strictly. Smoking is not allowed anywhere inside the building and food and drink is banned in the dormitories. Well, an invasive plant has the ability to spread aggressively outside its native range in a new habitat. Invasive plants can even cause economic or environmental harm. At the same time, they threaten local plants by competing for nutrients, light and water. Invasive species have contributed to the decline of many endangered and threatened species in the U.S. As many of you have noticed in your own life, some of these species outcompete other plants and take over a whole garden. So, they have become a serious problem that both the government and the public must deal with. These species are often brought out of their native range by humans or birds. They unknowingly carry the seeds with them to a new environment. Now let’s take a look at some invasive species and see how they are affecting native environment. Common Broom or Scotch Broom, is a plant native to western and central Europe. It typically grows to 1 to 3 meters tall. It is found in sunny sites. In America, this species has become an ecologically destructive plant, especially in grassland, shrubs and woodlands. It has a competitive advantage over native trees and shrubs in North America. And since its introduction, it has caused not only ecological but also economic problems. It even affected the performance of the commodity industry. It is estimated that it is responsible for the lost timber production which was worth $15 million US dollars last year in Oregon. As common broom can cause such a big problem, how can we control it? One way to start is by targeting the common broom plants that are producing fruits. Then we need to remove these fruit-bearing trees, and that will reduce the amount of seeds added to the soil each year. Another way is biological control, like introducing some insects from its place of origin. They will disturb the growth of this invasive plant. Next, there’s Japanese Barberry, which is native to Japan and eastern Asia. It tolerates a wide range of soil and moisture conditions. It is found along woodland edges, roadsides, stream banks, old fields and forests. This species was brought to America from Russia in 1975, and it is now widely seen throughout the US. It has yellow flowers and bears bright red fruits. It’s used widely as landscape and hedge material. It has been replacing native species in America. Furthermore, the plant can change soil condition and cause diseases to plants like wheat. In recent years, Japanese barberry has been recognized as an invasive species in many parts of the eastern United States. A variety of techniques including both mechanical and chemical controls may be effective in dealing with this species, but the exact method should be tailored to the specific conditions on the site. Buckthorn or Common Buckthorn, is a species of tree-like plant which usually grows two to three meters tall, but it occasionally reaches up to 10 meters tall. It has smooth, dark green leaves. Buckthorn can spread widely with the help of birds that eat its fruits. They then carry the seeds long distances along their path of migration. What can we do to control it? First, we need to learn how to identify common buckthorn. It is different from sea buckthorn, which is a plant that can be used to treat serious digestive problems. Then, we should avoid using it in gardens and landscape. You can contact the Invading Species Hotline if you find common buckthorn in the wild. So, let’s look at some pictures of these…

task1.title: Task 1: Report / Data Description
task1.prompt: The chart and table below show the proportion of energy generated from renewable and non-renewable sources in selected OECD countries between 2000 and 2020. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
task1.sampleBand8Answer:
The chart and accompanying table illustrate the comparative distribution of electricity production from renewable and conventional non-renewable sources across four OECD member nations—namely Germany, Sweden, Canada, and Japan—over a twenty-year timeframe from 2000 to 2020.

Overall, it is immediately apparent that all surveyed nations witnessed an upward trajectory in green energy adoption, with Sweden maintaining the foremost position in clean energy reliance throughout. Conversely, Japan continued to exhibit the lowest proportion of renewables despite moderate progress in the final decade.

In detail, Sweden commenced the period with 42% of its total energy coming from renewables in 2000, which subsequently expanded sharply to surpass 68% by 2020, driven primarily by investments in hydroelectric and wind installations. Canada similarly sustained high renewable dependency, starting at 56% and peaking at 64% by the end of the survey period.

In contrast, Germany underwent the most dramatic structural shift: renewable output represented a modest 8% in 2000 before quadrupling to approximately 39% in 2020 under comprehensive decarbonization initiatives. Japan, by comparison, began at just 7% and grew modestly to 18% in 2020, still leaving fossil and nuclear fuels to comprise the vast majority (82%) of its energy grid.

task2.title: Task 2: Academic Essay
task2.prompt: Some people believe that artificial intelligence and automation will bring massive unemployment and economic instability. Others argue that AI will foster innovation and create higher-value jobs. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
task2.sampleBand8Answer:
The rapid proliferation of artificial intelligence (AI) and robotic automation has ignited rigorous debate across global economic forums. While a considerable segment of the population expresses trepidation regarding widespread redundancy and fiscal volatility, others contend that this technological paradigm will unlock unprecedented productivity and cultivate novel vocational sectors. In my view, although transient displacement is inevitable, AI will ultimately function as a net positive catalyst for societal affluence.

On the one hand, apprehensions regarding job scarcity are grounded in historical precedent and empirical reality. In routine-intensive fields such as manufacturing, logistics, and entry-level clerical administration, autonomous algorithms execute quantitative computations and physical tasks with far greater velocity and precision than human operators. Consequently, unmitigated deployment without rigorous retraining frameworks risks marginalizing millions of low-skilled workers, thereby exacerbating wealth disparity and burdening public welfare reserves.

On the other hand, proponents persuasively assert that technological upheavals historically eliminate specific tasks rather than labor as a whole. By relieving human professionals of mundane, repetitive drudgery, automation creates capacity for higher-order cognitive domains such as ethical AI governance, specialized software architecture, and creative strategic consulting. Furthermore, empirical analyses indicate that machine-augmented industries stimulate secondary employment ecosystems—from renewable infrastructure to tailored biotechnology—which generate premium remuneration.

In conclusion, while the transition phase undeniably poses formidable challenges for specific occupational demographics, artificial intelligence represents a profound evolution rather than an existential crisis for the labor market. Governments and educational institutions must proactively orchestrate lifelong upskilling programs to ensure equitable participation in this automated era.

part2.title: Part 2: Individual Long Turn / Cue Card (3-4 mins)

cueCard.prompt: Describe a memorable professional or academic achievement that you are proud of.
bullets: When and where it took place
What challenges you had to overcome
And explain why you felt so proud of this accomplishment.

part2.sampleBand8Answer:
I would like to speak about a defining professional achievement from last year, when I successfully spearheaded the migration of our company's legacy customer management infrastructure to a secure cloud platform. This undertaking occurred over a grueling six-month period at our regional corporate headquarters.

The primary obstacle we confronted was the sheer complexity of legacy data formats, compounded by an unforgiving deployment deadline. We had to ensure zero downtime for over fifty thousand active global clients while synchronizing disparate legacy databases. Furthermore, midway through the project, several senior specialists had to quarantine due to seasonal health issues, which forced me to shoulder additional architectural duties and coordinate with offshore teams across multiple time zones.

Ultimately, the migration went live seamlessly without a single minute of service disruption. I felt immensely proud not only because the project cut infrastructure overhead by thirty percent, but because it substantiated my leadership capabilities under immense pressure and earned our team formal recognition from executive leadership.
